newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end slightly up, volume thin.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end slightly up, volume thin.

text.p: Key June three-month Euroyen futures ended Friday's TIFFE day session slightly higher in thin trade.
The June contract hit an intraday high of 99.23 following Japanese government bond (JGB) futures' jump in the early afternoon, traders said. The volume was 33,239 contracts.
December JGB futures ended at 124.75, up from 124.35 on Thursday but off its intraday high of 124.93.

JGB futures were boosted by news that Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto had agreed to work to reduce the government's planned bond issues for 1997/98 by more than three trillion yen.

"Euroyen futures were just following JGB futures' moves. The volume was very thin as market players were generally reluctant to set up new positions before the release of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) tankan next week," said a trader at a city bank.
The BOJ will release its key quarterly survey of corporate sentiment, known as the "tankan", on November 27.
Most experts expect the tankan's key diffusion index (DI) of major manufacturers to show only a modest improvement to around minus three or minus four from minus seven in the August tankan.
Traders said the market has already factored in a mild improvement in the headline DI.
"The market is watching carefully the BOJ's DI forecast for March 1997. If this number moves into positive territory, we may see selling," said a trader at another city bank.
Until the tankan release, June Euroyen futures are likely to remain between 99.20 and 99.25, he added.
The key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.49 percent, unchanged from Thursday.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 400 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
About 45 billion yen worth of two-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.51 percent, unchanged from the previous day.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, some players were showing interest on the receiving side in the two- to three-year sector, a city bank trader said.
